renderings.prompt: Wide cinematic exterior shot of a Minecraft build of the Cheyenne Mountain Complex NORAD bunker, viewed from a small gravel parking lot looking up at the cliff face. Massive 1,450-block-tall mountain made of pink-to-brick-red Pikes Peak granite (pink terracotta, red granite, polished andesite blocks), three-peaked silhouette with ponderosa pine forest (spruce trees) covering the lower slopes. A small, deliberately unassuming concrete-and-steel arch is set into the cliff face about 70% up the mountain — light grey concrete frame with iron-block corner caps, the words CHEYENNE MOUNTAIN COMPLEX in black block lettering across the top lintel, a small speed-limit-15 sign on a fence post. Chain-link iron fence with concertina wire chain coils flanks the approach. A small guardhouse sits to one side. Antenna arrays (iron block columns with lightning rods and chain cross-bracing) rise from the ridgeline against an overcast daylight sky. The mood is the 'paradox of the invisible building' — the bunker is hidden in plain sight, the mountain looks like a mountain. Cinematic Minecraft-block aesthetic, soft overcast daylight, slight haze in the air, professional concept visualization.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan cover image and section opener for the Exterior / Approach section. The hero shot the visitor sees first.

renderings.prompt: Interior first-person view inside a Minecraft build of the J-curve access tunnel of the Cheyenne Mountain Complex NORAD bunker. The visitor is standing in a curved tunnel cut from rough pink-to-brick-red Pikes Peak granite (pink terracotta, red granite, polished andesite blocks), looking down the curving passage. The tunnel walls are bare rock with iron-bar rock bolts in the ceiling, exposed color-coded utility pipes running along the lower walls (green concrete for water, red concrete for fire suppression, yellow concrete for fuel, blue concrete for compressed air), and oak-fence cable trays along the upper wall. The tunnel is lit by dim redstone-lamp ceiling strips every 10-15 blocks casting a cool blue-white fluorescent institutional light. The tunnel curves gently so the visitor CANNOT see the far end — this is the 'you cannot see where you are going' moment. The floor is polished andesite slabs with iron-trapdoor metal grating accents. A faint dark void is visible far ahead where the tunnel bends. The atmosphere is institutional, dim, quiet, slightly ominous — the 'dead air' feel of a sealed underground Cold War command center. Cinematic Minecraft-block aesthetic, atmospheric fog, professional concept visualization.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section opener for the Access Tunnel section. The 'you cannot see where you are going' moment.

renderings.prompt: Cinematic Minecraft build visualization of the blast door airlock at the Cheyenne Mountain Complex NORAD bunker — the threshold moment between outside and inside. A short curved side-branch tunnel of pink-to-brick-red Pikes Peak granite opens into an airlock chamber. Two massive 25-ton iron-block blast doors stand in sequence — the first door is open, the second door is closed, both angled outward at 5-10 degrees so blast pressure would push them shut. Each door is 6 blocks tall by 4 blocks wide, with black concrete frame, iron-bar chevron bracing, visible iron-bar hinges on the side, red concrete chevron warning stripes, and a chain column with an anvil hand-crank backup operator on the right. Between the doors, a small airlock chamber with light grey concrete walls, polished andesite floor, and a single dim redstone lamp providing dramatic backlight. An oak sign reads AIRLOCK. A second sign reads BLAST DOOR 25 TONS 30 MT @ 1.2 MI. The doors loom imposingly, framed by the rough pink granite of the side-branch tunnel behind. Dramatic cinematic lighting, the heavy industrial scale of the moment, 1966 institutional Air Force aesthetic, polished-andesite-and-iron-block palette. Cinematic Minecraft-block concept visualization.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section opener for the Threshold / Airlock section. The cinematic reveal moment.

renderings.prompt: The money shot — a Minecraft build visualization of the main chamber inside the Cheyenne Mountain Complex NORAD bunker. The chamber is lit by dim redstone lamp ceiling strips casting a cool blue-white fluorescent institutional glow. Cinematic Minecraft-block concept visualization, slightly dramatic atmospheric lighting from below, professional concept art quality.

renderings.prompt: Interior of the Battle Cab command center — a Minecraft build of the NORAD Combat Operations Center inside Cheyenne Mountain Complex. A vintage 2006-2016 institutional command room, not modern. U-shape of 6 operator consoles facing a wall of displays. The consoles are note blocks and jukeboxes with item-frame mosaic screens, each console paired with a light-grey-wool beige executive chair. The wall of displays dominates the front: a large central world map mosaic (item frames with map textures) flanked by status panel screens, with 7 clock blocks labeled with oak wall signs reading ZULU, EXERCISE, HAWAII, PACIFIC, MOUNTAIN, CENTRAL, EASTERN. Above the displays, a red banner reading WELCOME TO THE NORAD COMMAND CENTER in red concrete letters. The floor is blue wool carpet (institutional dark blue). A single large plaque on the back wall reads 'ON JUNE 3 1980 A 46-CENT COMPUTER CHIP FAILED IN THE MISSILE WARNING NETWORK. NORAD BRIEFLY REPORTED 2,200 SOVIET ICBMs INBOUND. BOMBER CREWS TOOK THEIR STATIONS. THE ALERT WAS RESOLVED WHEN A THIRD CALL REPORTED NO RADAR OR SATELLITE CONFIRMATION.' The room is dimly lit by redstone lamp ceiling fixtures with cool fluorescent glow, the screens casting the dominant light. The atmosphere is the 'dead air' feel of a 1980s command center — institutional grey, dim, slightly haunted by the weight of the decisions made here. Cinematic Minecraft-block concept visualization.
renderings.intended_use: Master plan section opener for the Battle Cab / Command Center section. The visual climax of the visitor's walk-through.
